title: Vibration Isolation Solutions for S/TEM
content: Vibration is an omnipresent phenomenon in our environment, affecting various types of microscopes, particularly the ultra-sensitive Scanning Electron Microscopes (SEM) and Transmission Electron Microscopes (TEM). To mitigate these effects, S/TEM manufacturers incorporate passive isolation systems that utilize springs—such as metal springs, rubber dampers, or air springs—to reduce high-frequency vibrations. While these passive systems effectively isolate vibrations above the resonance frequency of the spring-mass system, they do not address all frequency ranges. Additionally, they cannot be optimized regardless of the specific environmental conditions in which the instrument is situated. For instance, an S/TEM located on the top floor of a building will experience greater floor vibrations compared to one positioned in the basement. The variability architecture of buildings is another large factor and of course geography can influence the spectra at a site. A large subset of all possible site parameters leads to insufficient isolation even at frequencies above the resonance frequency of the passive system. S/TEM manufacturers will list out the floor vibration specifications that need to be maintained for the microscope to operate properly.
